content.comment_body: I'm running a 4-day test program, and some steps involve waiting for 40 minutes. I'd like to bypass or quickly move past these lengthy steps. Is there any method to speed up the simulation? Thanks! I am working with [product_name] [version_no].
You can't alter the simulation speed itself. However, you can adjust the timer values used during simulation.
That was what I was trying to avoid. Thanks!
No, it's not possible to change simulation speed directly. As a workaround, you could duplicate your program and set the timers to shorter durations, like converting hours to seconds.

Hello, you can actually adjust the time in simulation mode. On the status line, there's a clock icon; clicking it allows you to change the simulation’s date and time, but these changes only remain until you restart the simulation. Additionally, single and multiple cycle simulations are possible in [product_name] simulation. I’ve attached a picture of the simulation status bar. Hope this is helpful.

Hi [user_name], for me, this doesn’t really increase simulation speed. Adjusting the clock helps the process end faster, but what about elements like storage being reset by an elapsed timer? In simulation mode, timers operate normally, so changing the time doesn’t affect them—except for things like weekly or yearly timers.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for ways to accelerate simulation speed in [product_name] [version_no] to avoid lengthy waits during test scenarios involving timers. Directly speeding up or skipping steps isn't available, so most rely on manually reducing timer durations or adjusting the simulated clock—both approaches come with limitations. There is debate on whether these changes truly meet their needs, indicating a lack of clarity and comprehensive guidance within the available documentation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the ability to configure or fast-forward simulation speed within the software, allowing quick and efficient validation of processes that span long durations—without needing to alter timers repeatedly or use complicated workarounds.
